result.summary: This PR closes a race in Bitcoin Core's connection manager where concurrent -connect and -addnode attempts at startup can both pass the existing duplicate-connection checks (which only see peers already in m_nodes) and open two sockets to the same manual peer. It fixes this by reserving a normalized destination key in OpenNetworkConnection() before dialing, releasing the reservation on failure or once the node is published to m_nodes. The fix is scoped to ConnectionType::MANUAL only, and a new functional test (p2p_duplicate_manual_connections.py) reproduces the startup race and fails without the fix. This is a rework ("take 2") of a previously closed approach (#27804) that de-duplicated CLI arguments instead of tracking in-flight attempts.
result.problem: Node operators who configure the same peer via both -connect and -addnode (or trigger overlapping manual reconnection/RPC connection attempts) can end up with duplicate outbound connections to that peer, wasting a connection slot and potentially confusing peer accounting, because the existing dedup logic only checks already-established peers.

result.card: This PR fixes a startup race in Bitcoin Core's net.cpp where -connect and -addnode can concurrently dial the same peer and both succeed, because existing duplicate checks only see peers already inserted into m_nodes. The fix reserves a normalized manual-connection key in OpenNetworkConnection() before dialing and releases it on failure or once the peer is published, scoped only to ConnectionType::MANUAL. It closes long-open issue #5299 and is a reworked, less-brittle version of a previously closed PR (#27804). A new functional regression test reproduces the race and fails without the fix. So far it has only two concept ACKs (sedited, w0xlt) and no detailed code review; nothing blocks review starting now, though a hostname-keying limitation (not DNS-resolved) is a known, author-acknowledged tradeoff worth scrutiny.
